prompt: What is the median of the data set $4$, $7$, $9$, $12$, $15$, $20$?
hint: Count the values in the list. When the count is even, no single value sits exactly in the middle.

hints.text: Count the values in the list. When the count is even, no single value sits exactly in the middle.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try four values: for $2, 4, 6, 8$ the middle two are $4$ and $6$, so the median is $5$. With an even count you average the middle pair.
The list is in order and has six values, so the middle pair is the third and fourth values, $9$ and $12$. Find the average of that pair.
The average is $\dfrac{9 + 12}{2} = 10.5$, so the median is $10.5$.

learningObjective: Find the median of an even-sized data set.
explanation: The data are already in order, and with $6$ values the middle two are the third and fourth: $9$ and $12$.
For an even number of values the median is the average of the middle pair: $\dfrac{9 + 12}{2} = 10.5$.
The median is $10.5$, even though that number is not itself in the data set.

alternativeExplanations.title: Locating the middle pair
steps: For $n$ values with $n$ even, the middle two sit at positions $\dfrac{n}{2}$ and $\dfrac{n}{2} + 1$.
Here $n = 6$, so positions $3$ and $4$ — the values $9$ and $12$.
Counting inward from both ends simultaneously is the practical version of this, and it is harder to miscount.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Answering 9 or 12 — either middle value alone — is the designed error for even-sized sets.
An even count has no single middle: average the middle PAIR. The median of this set is 10.5, a number not even in the data.
